title: Prompt anchoring consensus fanout CI adapter with latency-aware soft-throttle
author: Anika Patel
description: Context: We observed intermittent prompt-set regressions that only show up when a small fraction of traffic triggers a different prompt variant; existing cohort gates are too coarse and either over-block or miss subtle regressions. This PR introduces a CI adapter (Prompt Anchoring Consensus Fanout) that fans out a small, configurable fraction of CI-eval traffic to multiple anchoring strategies, aggregates a consensus signal across them, and applies a latency-aware soft-throttle when disagreement or latency drift exceed thresholds. Motivation: reduce noisy false-positives while catching low-signal regressions early, and avoid large-scale CI failures driven by transient latency spikes. Design summary: 1) Fanout layer: routes evaluation jobs to 3 anchoring strategies (lexical anchor, semantic shingle anchor, and recent-traffic replay) in parallel. 2) Consensus aggregator: computes a consensus score (weighted majority with tie-breaker using confidence) and emits a composite regression score. 3) Latency-aware soft-throttle: if regression score crosses the soft-fail threshold but median latency for the eval backends exceeds a configured SLO, the adapter returns a soft-throttle (CI warning) instead of a hard failure. 4) Canary and rollouts: adapter supports a phased rollout via config flags: enabled=false by default, canary=true to enable for 3% of CI runs, then ramp. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4721) [x] unit tests for aggregator logic [x] e2e smoke tests in local harness [x] CI integration tests (mocked backends) [x] metrics + tracing added [x] console toggles & feature flag gating [x] rollout plan in PR description Compatibility: adapter integrates with existing eval orchestration via a light extension point (EvalRunner::post_process_hooks). Backwards compatibility preserved when the adapter is disabled. Testing notes: - deterministic-unit tests for consensus weighting (seeded RNG) - synthetic noise experiments show false-positive rate drop ~45% compared to single-anchor gating on our sampled prompt-sets - latency soft-throttle prevented 3/4 of recent spurious hard blocks during 72h replay. Rollout plan: enable canary in CI for internal main branch builds (3% traffic) for 48h, monitor composite regression metric and alert on >2x false positive or >1.2x missed regression rate; escalate to roll back flag if needed. Related: Linear ENG-4721 (design), ENG-4890 (canary dashboard).

review_comments: Devin Shaw: Nice approach. Two questions: 1) how do we pick the weights for each anchor? 2) can the soft-throttle leak a false 'pass' under heavy load?

Anika Patel (author): We pick initial weights from historical anchor fidelity (stored in eval metadata) and expose a config param for linear decay during canary. Soft-throttle design uses median latency and only downgrades hard failures to warnings; it will not convert a clear regression into a pass — it downgrades immediate CI blocking to a soft block and creates a follow-up probe job for longer-running verification.
Marcus Li: Needs more telemetry around per-anchor false positives so SRE can diagnose. Also please ensure spans have the eval_id tag for trace correlation.
Anika Patel: Added metrics "anchor.fp_rate", "anchor.tp_rate", and ensured trace span includes eval_id and prompt_set_id. Added to instrumentation commit.
Priya Shah: test coverage looks good, but can we add one flaky-simulation test where one anchor is malicious/outlier and ensure consensus recovers?
Anika Patel: added a unit test simulating an adversarial anchor that flips labels; consensus recovers in >95% of sampled trials (test_consensus.py).
merge_commit_message: Add anchoring consensus fanout adapter + latency-aware soft-throttle (ENG-4721)
release_notes: Introduces a feature-flagged CI adapter that fans out evals to multiple anchoring strategies and computes a consensus regression score. Includes a latency-aware soft-throttle to reduce noisy hard CI failures. Disabled by default; enable via feature flag and follow rollout guide in docs/operations/anchoring_consensus.md.
post_merge_tasks: Enable canary flag for internal CI (3%)
Create dashboard panel (ENG-4890) to track composite regression score and anchor-level false positive rates
Schedule 48h review after canary to decide ramping
notes_for_qa: Run tests with --seed=42 for deterministic consensus behavior. For e2e, use the provided mocked backend profiles in tests/e2e/profiles/. To simulate latency soft-throttle, inject median backend latency > 1200ms in the smoke harness.
notes_from_release: No behavioral changes to production pipelines when feature flag is off. Monitoring will show additional metrics once enabled.
additional_context: This PR was developed in response to a recurrence of Flaky CI incidents logged in ENG-4320. The approach borrows ideas from ensemble methods and is intentionally conservative: the adapter errs on the side of warnings during early rollout.
acknowledgements: Thanks to the SRE triage team (Liam O'Connor) for incident context and to Research (Sofia Reyes) for anchoring evaluation scripts.
